figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Biosynthesis of ATAAs in fungi. (A) 2-Aminoisobutyric acid (AIB, 1) and L-isovaline (L-2) are biosynthesized from L-valine and L-
isoleucine, respectively, through the actions of TqaL/F/M. (B) The previously proposed reaction mechanism, based on an in vitro analysis and 18O-
labeling experiment.30

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Stereospecificity analysis of TqaM. (A) The structures of
substrates. (B and C) HPLC analyses of the enzymatic reaction
products of (B) TaTqaM with (S)-3, (R)-3, and 5 and (C) TaTqaM
with (2R,3S)-4 and (2R,3R)-4. Compounds 1, 2, and 5 were derivatized
by dansyl chloride, and 4 was derivatized by Nα-(5-fluoro-2,4-
dinitrophenyl)-L-alaninamide (FDAA) for detection.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Comparison of the active site entrances of TqaMs. The
active site entrances of (A) PaTqaM in complex with (R)-3, (B)
TaTqaM in complex with AIB, (C) TaTqaM apo, and (D) PaTqaM in
complex with (R)-6. Orange and purple spheres represent Fe2+ and
Mn2+, respectively. The N-terminal loops covering the active site are
shown as sticks. The loop regions between Ser178 and Ala187 in
PaTqaM and Asp158−Ala167 in TaTqaM are colored purple, blue,
yellow, and green in panels A−D, respectively.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Substrate and product binding in TqaM. The active sites of
(A) PaTqaM in complex with (R)-3 and (B) TaTqaM in complex with
1. Compounds (R)-3 and 1 are represented by blue and white sticks,
respectively. Metal coordination and hydrogen bonding interactions are
shown as blue and yellow bonds, respectively. Distances are given in
Angstroms. Green and magenta residues are from monomer A, while
gray residues are from the adjacent monomer. (C) Mutagenesis
experiment of TqaM active site residues, with WT indicating the wild
type. All reactions were performed in triplicate. Data are presented as
mean values, and error bars indicate the standard deviation (SD) from
triplicate experiments.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Substrate specificity analysis of PaTqaM-Δ23. Enzymatic
reactions of PaTqaM-Δ23 with (A) phenylic substrate analogues (R)-6
and (R)-7, (B) C3-tertiarily substituted C2-hydroxy compounds (11−
15), and (C) 3-monosubstituted β-amino acids (21−23) and 3,3-
disubstituted β-amino acids (24−29) as substrates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Comparison of the active sites between PaTqaM in complex with (R)-3 and (R)-6. (A) Superimposed view of PaTqaM in complex with
(R)-3 and (R)-6. The N-terminal loops in the (R)-3 and (R)-6 binding structures are represented by gray and blue sticks, respectively. (B and C)
Comparison of substrate binding modes of (B) (R)-3 (yellow sticks) and (C) (R)-6 (orange sticks).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Enzymatic synthesis of non-proteinogenic amino acids. (A) Enzymatic reactions of PaTqaM-Δ23 with 3-monosubstituted β-amino acids
(21−23) as substrates. Compounds 21 and 30 were derivatized with FDAA and detected at 254 nm UV. Compounds 22 and 31 were derivatized with
dansyl chloride for detection. (B) Enzymatic reactions of PaTqaM-Δ23 with 3,3-disubstituted β-amino acids (24−29) as substrates.
